evidence.VOTE: On 18 November 2024 at the Security Council's 9786th meeting, draft S/2024/826, submitted by Sierra Leone and the United Kingdom, received 14 votes in favour, one against and no abstentions. China voted in favour. The Russian Federation cast the sole negative vote. The Council did not adopt the draft because a permanent member voted against.
evidence.TEXT: The proposed text concerned ending hostilities in Sudan, protecting civilians and facilitating humanitarian access. The vote did not adopt these measures in S/2024/826.
evidence.RU-A: Dmitry Polyanskiy criticized the proposed text as creating a route for outside interference in Sudan. He opposed using external accountability mechanisms and argued that administration of justice should remain with the Government of Sudan.
evidence.RU-B: Polyanskiy argued that humanitarian measures needed agreement with Sudan's central authorities. He called for time and political space for Personal Envoy Ramtane Lamamra to engage relevant actors.
evidence.CN-A: Fu Cong supported an immediate ceasefire and de-escalation to protect civilians and explained that this was why China voted in favour. He also said some constructive proposals and concerns had not been fully reflected.
evidence.CN-B: Fu emphasized Sudanese sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity, and said Council action should rest on consultation with Sudan's Government and other relevant parties. He supported the Personal Envoy's coordination with the African Union and regional organizations.
